target.title: Clear derived provider state when disabling providers
target.body:
## Summary

- clear provider-derived runtime state when a provider is disabled or becomes unavailable
- invalidate in-flight usage, status, token-cost, and cached-hydration work so stale completions cannot republish after disable, re-enable, or provider configuration changes
- retain explicit allow-disabled verification behavior and retry only the exact stale token-cost lanes
- preserve provider settings, account configuration, historical data, and durable caches owned by their existing lifetimes

## Proof

- `swift test --filter 'UsageStoreDisabledProviderCleanupTests|ProviderRefreshCoordinatorTests|UsageStoreCachedTokenHydrationTests|CodexManagedRoutingTests|SettingsStoreCoverageTests'` — 93 tests passed
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuInstantOpenTests` — 29 tests passed
- `make check` — SwiftFormat clean; SwiftLint 0 violations across 1,409 files
- `CODEXBAR_TEST_RETRY_NON_TIMEOUT_FAILURES=0 make test` — all 628 selections passed first attempt across 53 groups; 0 retries and 0 timeouts
- autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings
- exact signed debug bundle — embedded commit `fcac7722`; strict code-sign verification and Gatekeeper acceptance passed
- source-blind isolated app proof — real Settings enable/disable/re-enable, clean disabled menu, no stale success after re-enable, and disabled persistence across exact-bundle relaunch all passed; production app process remained unchanged

target.title: Avoid duplicate Agent Sessions remote refresh passes
target.body:
## Summary
- Coalesce unchanged overlapping Agent Sessions remote refresh requests into the active pass instead of scheduling a duplicate Tailscale discovery and SSH sweep.
- Preserve generation invalidation, stale-result suppression, and one immediate retry when Agent Sessions settings change during a pass.
- Add focused gate coverage and document the user-visible efficiency fix with contributor credit.

## Validation
- Exact head: `61cdbdc21983fa0902406df14a2f28c1defa636c`, synchronized with current `main`.
- Focused Agent Sessions/Tailscale and synchronized-main suites: 115/115 passed.
- Settings-change gate proof: stale generation is not published and exactly one current-generation retry follows.
- `make check`: generated docs, locale checks, SwiftFormat, and SwiftLint clean.
- Zero-retry full suite: 624/624 selections across 52/52 groups, all first-pass; no retries or timeouts.
- Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; 0.96 correctness confidence.
- Exact Developer ID-signed debug bundle: embedded commit `61cdbdc2`; strict code-sign and Gatekeeper accepted.
- Packaged live app with isolated config, Keychain disabled, and local no-network Tailscale/SSH wrappers: five menu opens completed in 2.028 seconds during one blocked pass; counts stayed at discovery/fetch `1/0`, then settled at `1/1`; the menu rendered `qa-host — 1` / `qa-shared`.
- Production CodexBar PID, executable path, start time, and restored debug defaults remained unchanged.

## Risk
Low. Concurrent callers now share an active remote failure instead of forcing an immediate duplicate pass; the next menu open or normal 60-second cycle retries. Settings changes still force one current-generation pass.

## Dependencies
No dependency changes; freshness review not applicable.

target.title: fix(docs): reorder AGENTS.md template to protect critical rules from truncation
target.body:
fix(docs): reorder AGENTS.md template to protect critical rules from truncation

## Summary
**Problem:** The auto-generated `AGENTS.md` template puts personality/onboarding guidance (First Run, Session Startup, Memory) at the top and safety-critical rules (Red Lines, External vs Internal) at the bottom. When `bootstrapMaxChars` truncates from the head, the safety rules are stripped while less-critical content is preserved.

**Fix:** Reorder the template so Red Lines and External vs Internal appear immediately after the title, before First Run/Session Startup/Memory. Head-truncation now preserves the most operationally-critical guidance.

**Out of scope:** No changes to truncation logic, bootstrapMaxChars behavior, or content-aware truncation. Only reorders the template.

## Linked context
Closes #75187

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: AGENTS.md template orders safety rules after personality content, so head-truncation by bootstrapMaxChars strips the rules
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node.js v22.11.0, OpenClaw latest main (commit 3a64302, 2026-06-03)
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Read the reordered template and verified Red Lines section appears at line 12 (before Memory at line 44)
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output showing the reordered template structure:
```
$ head -20 docs/reference/templates/AGENTS.md
---
summary: "Workspace template for AGENTS.md"
title: "AGENTS.md template"
read_when:
  - Bootstrapping a workspace manually
---

# AGENTS.md - Your Workspace

This folder is home. Treat it that way.

## Red Lines

- Don't exfiltrate private data. Ever.
- Don't run destructive commands without asking.
- Before changing config or schedulers (for example crontab, systemd units, nginx configs, or shell rc files), inspect existing state first and preserve/merge by default.
- `trash` > `rm` (recoverable beats gone forever)
- When in doubt, ask.

## External vs Internal
```
- Observed result after fix: Red Lines is now at line 12 (was at line 61). External vs Internal is at line 20 (was at line 69). With `bootstrapMaxChars: 1500`, the first ~1500 chars now include both safety sections.
- What was not tested: Live gateway bootstrap with small model (requires full OpenClaw setup)

## Tests and validation
- No code changes, only template reordering
- No CHANGELOG.md edits

## Risk checklist
- userVisible: Yes (AGENTS.md template order changes for new workspaces)
- configEnvMigration: No
- securityAuthNetwork: No
- Mitigation: Only reorders existing content, no content removed or added
